Campaign planning is almost as much fun as DM'ing it to my party.

Agreed. I really enjoy building my dungeons and crafting my NPC's backgrounds and motivations...

Too bad my players just head in the opposite direction and never see any of it. haha

Yeah, pulling off a homemade dungeon/adventure you worked on and having your players tell you it was fun is incredibly satisfying.

I had that problem too. It does remind me of a quote though: "Bad DM's railroad. Good DM's railroad subtly." The trick is to get them back on track while they still think they are doing something totally unrelated.

Definitely, I like that quote. I kind of follow the philosophy in my homebrew of building a functional world and setting and letting the players experience it however they want. Build a setting and people who live in that setting, and let your NPC's start affecting other NPC's and settings... There's definitely a lot happening on a grand scale in the campaign, and that means that eventually your players will get involved in it, in one way or another.

That's very true. My group is currently going from a premade setting (Forgotten realms; we started with the Lost Mines Premade), and are currently about to start in my new homebrew I'm making. Their characters in the FR were fighting a cleric and basically had their souls ripped out and tossed into a new plane of existance. Their new characters were the (un?)lucky people who just got an additional soul shoved into them.

The plan is to have them start in this 'new' world and do a more free-range style adventure.

So your players are playing new characters that house both the souls of their new characters AND the souls of their old characters? Schizo style? That's the greatest thing I've ever read. That will be a fun campaign!

Yep! The plan is that they will be new personalities that slowly rediscover their past lives. So every time they level up they will have the opportunity to 'import' skills, languages, and abilities (including spells if both the old and new characters are magic users) on top of their normal leveling up stuff. They retain all their old memories from the get-go though.

They just finished the end of the last campaign just the other night, so i'm knee deep in figuring out all the fine mechanics of the reincarnation stuff. My players are all pretty good (been playing together weekly for ~10 months), so it should be a fun time indeed.

I tried something new recently and had my players help generate everything for the world they were about to go in. I had a checklist of basic information to get from them and even had them draw their own world map. End result? They had a blast! They were having so much fun with it that I came up with several random tables for monsters/NPCs and such for them to fill out as well to keep it going. Anyways, your post made me think of this as one of them even said it was almost as much fun creating the world as it was playing later.
That sounds pretty fun! I have some unfinished areas of my world left, so I may try that and see how they handle building another nation or something.
